summary: 2D screening label: illustrative_2d_only. Studio did not run (simulation status 'skipped'; simulation_allowed=false). The gate failed because the custom 2D steady experiment has an empty floorplan and no power_w object, so the input is invalid (input_gate_pass=false, scientific_gate_pass=false, independently_verified=false). comparison_valid=false. The scenario is the Fig. 1 motivational example: an 8x8 Alpha 21264 array at 22 nm, 2.6 GHz, 50% dark cores, running multi-thread H.264 in steady state with HotSpot v5.02 and McPAT power. The paper reports per-pattern chip peaks of 80.67, 82.17, 82.15, 75.67, 80.11 and 72.81 C against Tsafe = 81.8 C. Patterns 2 and 3 exceed the threshold, and the uniform pattern 6 is lowest. These are paper-reported values only, not reproduced. Since no simulation ran, there is no Studio temperature, no transient trace (this is a steady-state request) and no numerical comparison with the paper. Qualitatively, the paper reports that spreading active cores apart, so each is surrounded by dark cores, lowers the peak versus contiguous activation. This is the paper's own finding and was not checked here. No pinned assets exist (no Ascend910 or ATPlace commit, no generated placement and no input.flp or input.ptrace), so there is no source commit or placement assumption to report. The result must not be read as an exact replication or validation of the paper.

Not a 3D, interposer or chiplet stack. The scenario is a monolithic 2D homogeneous core array, so interposer, 3D and chiplet-floorplan thermal effects are not represented.

The paper's optimizer (ILP/TopoMap task mapping on a SMART NoC with bypass routing) and runtime MatEx transient control are not part of the Fig. 1 steady-state HotSpot scenario, so optimizer and controller behavior cannot be reproduced from it.

No per-core x/y/width/height geometry and no per-core wattage are published. Only the array size (8x8), the 50% dark fraction and peak temperatures are given, so floorplan and power inputs cannot be reconstructed.

The cooling and package model is given only partially in Table 2 (HotSpot parameters). Chip thickness 0.15 mm, heat sink convection resistance 0.1 K/W and ambient 318.15 K are listed. Die dimensions, spreader and sink geometry, and package layers are not given, which limits solver fidelity.
Pattern-specific active-core locations are shown only graphically in Fig. 1. They are not tabulated and would have to be digitized with uncertainty.
Reliability is addressed only through the Tsafe = 81.8 C threshold. There is no lifetime or electromigration model.

No pinned assets or code are supplied, so any Studio package would use its own bundled 2D steady-state thermal solver and default material and package properties, which are not the paper's HotSpot v5.02 grid model.

The only paper-published thermal inputs usable as Studio assumptions are the Table 2 values: silicon conductivity 100 W/m-K, chip thickness 0.15 mm, spreader conductivity 400 W/m-K, and ambient 318.15 K (45 C).

An illustrative 2D placement of an 8x8 array with a one-row power trace may be generated only as a separate construction. Generated coordinates and powers must be labeled as non-paper-derived, and its temperatures must not be compared numerically with the paper's Fig. 1 peaks.
Dark cores are assumed to have zero power, as stated in the paper (PDF page 12).
